newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM's party faces major split ahead of polls.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM's party faces major split ahead of polls.

text.p: The Thai premier's fractious Chart Thai party faced mass defections after his surprise call for snap elections while the main opposition Democrat party was set to gain most from the polls, analysts said on Saturday.

Banharn Silpa-archa's gamble could break up his 91-seat Chart Thai party as it had angered some factions who had wanted him to hand over his job to rival and Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, they said.
The outgoing prime minister, whose integrity was mauled in a no-confidence debate against him in parliament 10 days ago, dissolved his six-party coalition and the House of Representatives on Friday.

Chavalit, ambitious leader of 57-seat New Aspiration Party (NAP), had been behind a demand last Saturday by coalition parties for Banharn to announce his resignation in exchange for their support to help him win the no-confidence vote.
Banharn kept coalition partners and the opposition guessing for a week about next moves before he dropped the election bombshell on Friday.
Analysts said the Chart Thai Party could see about half of its elected politicians defecting to other parties.

Among those expected to desert Chart Thai are 10 to 15 members of parliament led by party secretary-general and Public Health Minister Sanoh Thienthong. He may run in the November 17 polls under the NAP banner.
"One of the most important qualities of politicians is keeping promises. Without it, they're nothing," Sanoh said on Friday referring to Banharn's decision to call an election.
More than 20 other Chart Thai members led by former Deputy Interior Minister Suchart Tancharoen and former Deputy Finance Minister Newin Chidchob are also likely to seek new party alliances.

Chart Thai spokesman Somsak Prisana-anantakul said on Saturday Banharn had no plan to quit as party leader and was determined to revive its popularity among urban voters and businessmen after serious setbacks in the past 14 months.

The Democrats, led by former Prime Minister Chuan Leekpai, held an early election strategy meeting on Saturday. Party spokesmen were confident that they would replace Chart Thai as the bigggest bloc in parliament by winning more than the 86 seats captured in the last elections in July 1995.

Analysts said Chavalit's well-financed NAP could also outperform Chart Thai in the polls as it would be strengthened by defectors from Chart Thai and other smaller parties in Banharn's outgoing coalition.
Chavalit's position was also boosted by the annual reshuffle of the Thai military in mid-September when his allies were promoted to commanders of key army units.
But the analysts and opposition MPs said the prime minister, a 20-year veteran of Thai politics, had made preparations in the past week that would help his party in the polls.
Banharn has ordered sweeping changes of senior police and interior ministry officials who will be charged with supervising the elections.
He also tried to woo voters on Friday by appointing seven respected active and retired civil servants as caretaker ministers responsible for reviving a slowing economy and sluggish exports.
